subject: Orchid AI — proposal for utilization-triggered GPU scaling & renewal path
messages:
From: Liza Chen <liza@orchid.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal window + flexible scaling idea

Jordan —

We’re starting the renewal conversation for our Dedicated fleet (current commit: 120 A100-GPU equivalents) and the Q2 usage report is attached. Usage was higher than our forecasted baseline for two short windows in May — peak sustained for ~48 hours.

Before we jump to a straight top-up, curious if Redwood can propose a renewal path that lets us keep a conservative baseline commit but automatically brings on extra capacity when our utilization signal crosses a threshold.

Key asks from our side:
- A clear trigger definition so Procurement can approve (metric, window, minimum duration)
- Billing model for triggered capacity (pro-rated, monthly, overage vs reserved tranche)
- A rollback/fallback plan if utilization drops or model behavior changes

Attaching orchid_q2_util_report.csv for context. Happy to hop on a short call this week.

Cheers,
Liza Chen
Head of ML Ops | Orchid AI
Liza@orchid.ai

(Attachment: orchid_q2_util_report.csv)

From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Liza Chen <liza@orchid.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + flexible scaling idea

Hi Liza —

Thanks for the report — useful visibility. We can propose a utilization-triggered renewal path that maps to your procurement constraints while keeping unit economics predictable. High-level proposal attached (RDW-8721-elastic-trigger-proposal.pdf). Summary here: 

- Trigger metric: 7-day moving average of per-GPU token-service utilization (percent of sustained compute occupancy).
- Trigger threshold: default 72% (configurable). Trigger fires if threshold exceeded for 48 continuous hours.
- Action: automatically provision a pre-agreed tranche (example: +12 GPU-equivalents) pulled from a reserved burst pool; capacity becomes reserved for the remainder of the monthly billing period, then re-evaluated at monthly reconciliation.
- Billing: triggered tranche is billed pro-rata for the month as a reserved tranche (not overage), at a discounted rate vs on-demand but slightly above base commit unit price.
- Safeguards: cap at 2 concurrent triggered tranches, automatic cooldown of 7 days after a downscale, and an emergency manual override to avoid unexpected charges.

Next steps: if this aligns conceptually, Marissa will share a cost scenario and Karthik will confirm the measurement and enforcement details. Can we schedule a 30-min slot tomorrow?

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: RDW-8721-elastic-trigger-proposal.pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Liza Chen <liza@orchid.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + flexible scaling idea — measurement specifics

Looping in the technical bits so procurement has clarity. Notes / recommendations: 

- Metric definition: per-GPU sustained occupancy measured as average GPU SM utilization weighted by active inference time (exclude idle intervals <5s to avoid noise). Use a 7-day simple moving average (SMA7).
- Threshold window: require SMA7 > 72% for a rolling 48-hour contiguous window (this avoids single-day spikes).
- Provisioning unit: tranches are offered in GPU-equivalents (we normalize to A100x1 units). Example tranche sizes: 6, 12, 24.
- Reservation enforcement: provisioned tranches come from your pre-purchased burst pool. If burst pool is exhausted, we fall back to on-demand with an explicit pre-approved cap and notification.
- Telemetry: we’ll provide daily dashboard snapshots and a reconciliation export at month end (CSV + signed usage statement for procurement).

Operational caveat: if your workload shifts (e.g., longer sequence lengths or higher cache-hit variance), nominal utilization can rise without proportional inference throughput change. Recommend an initial pilot (90 days) with a single small tranche (6 GPUs) to validate the signal and economics.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liza Chen <liza@orchid.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + flexible scaling idea — pricing scenarios

Hi all —

Per the pilot approach, attached is a short cost scenarios sheet and an illustrative invoice cadence. Key numbers below are rough estimates (finals will be in the contract addendum):

Scenario A — Conservative baseline + small elastic tranche (pilot)
- Baseline commit: 120 GPUs (current) — keep unchanged for 90 days.
- Pilot tranche: +6 GPUs (reserved when triggered).
- Trigger billing: pro-rated reserved tranche at 0.85x baseline commit unit price (vs your committed unit).
- Estimated Q3 impact (based on orchid_q2_util_report.csv): +$18k/mo when active; expected active days ~12/month for current seasonality.

Scenario B — Modest baseline reduction + elastic tranches
- Baseline commit: reduce to 110 GPUs; allow 2x 12-GPU tranches.
- Billing: baseline discounted commit rate; tranches billed at 0.9x commit rate.
- Estimated net delta: neutral to slightly positive vs current spend depending on how frequently triggers fire.

Contract items we’ll include: clear reconciliation export, monthly trigger audit, cap on total triggered spend (procurement-settable), and a 30-day termination window for tranche scheduling changes.

Action items for Orchid:
1) Confirm whether Procurement requires a hard predictable monthly cap or is comfortable with capped-trigger spend.
2) If acceptable, procurement to share PO template and signatory details; we’ll draft an addendum for the 90-day pilot.

—Marissa Cole
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: RDW-8721-cost-scenarios.xlsx)

From: Liza Chen <liza@orchid.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchid.ai
Date: 2028-06-20T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + flexible scaling idea — confirming pilot

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks — the proposal and scenarios are clear. Procurement reviewed and we’re willing to proceed with the 90-day pilot (deal RDW-8721) with the following agreed points: 

- Pilot start date: 2028-07-01.
- Baseline commit held at 120 GPUs for pilot.
- Pilot tranche: +6 GPUs, trigger = SMA7 > 72% for 48hrs.
- Billing: pro-rated reserved tranche at 0.85x commit unit price when active.
- Monthly reconciliation and a signed usage export to procurement.
- Hard cap: $40k/month on total triggered spend during pilot (procurement requirement).

Please send a short addendum and the PO template and we’ll get signatures in the next 5 business days. Also, assign a technical contact on your side for dashboard access.

Liza
Liza Chen
Head of ML Ops | Orchid AI
procurement@orchid.ai
